subject: Social Habits
title: Eating manners
objectives: Children will wash hands before eating and sit to eat.
Children will say please and thank you at mealtimes.
content: Washing hands before eating, sitting and eating nicely, and not wasting food.
teachingActivities: Check allergies and dietary needs before any food activity; use real snack time where possible; never force a child to eat; respect families’ ways of eating (with hands, spoons or forks) and food customs; keep a second adult nearby for choking safety; avoid whole nuts, hard sweets and other choking hazards.
learnerActivities: Wash hands before eating, sit to eat and say please and thank you at mealtimes.
resources: A play kitchen or toy food
assessment: Observe whether each child washes hands before eating, sits to eat and says thank you.
expectedOutcomes: Washes hands before eating with support.
Sits to eat and says thank you.

lessons.title: Washing hands before eating
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will wash their hands before eating.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can care for belongings and use please and thank you.
lessons.starter: Show a plate of toy food and say "Before we eat, we wash our hands."
teacherActivities: Show how to wash hands with soap and rub.
Dry hands on a clean towel.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to wash hands with soap and rub. Children: Children watch and copy.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the hand washing song. Children: Children sing and rub.
Step 3. Teacher: Dry hands on a clean towel. Children: Child dries hands.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Clean hands before food." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Clean hands for food
practical.safety: Use mild soap and shallow water and wipe spills. Supervise every child at the basin.

differentiation.support: Wash hands together with a hand over the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remind a friend to wash.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do before we eat?

lessons.conclusion: Show clean hands and say "Ready to eat."
lessons.homeConnection: Wash hands together before every meal.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "wash their hands before eating" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?

lessons.title: Sitting and eating nicely
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will sit at a table and eat nicely.
successCriteria: Sits at the table to eat
Chews with the mouth closed with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can care for belongings and use please and thank you.
resources: Toy food or a small safe snack
lessons.starter: Set a small table and say "We sit down to eat. We do not run with food."
teacherActivities: Show how to sit with feet down and pull your chair in.
Show eating slowly with a closed mouth.
Say "Please may I have some?" and "Thank you."
Say "We eat slowly and stay seated."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to sit with feet down and pull your chair in. Children: Children sit at the table.
Step 2. Teacher: Show eating slowly with a closed mouth. Children: Children copy with toy food.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Please may I have some?" and "Thank you." Children: Child asks and thanks.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We eat slowly and stay seated." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Table manners
practical.safety: Use toy food for practice or only soft safe foods after checking allergies. A second adult must watch for choking at all times.

differentiation.support: Eat beside the child and copy together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the host who serves friends.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sits at the table to eat
Uses please and thank you at the table
lessons.conclusion: Wipe the table and say "Thank you."
lessons.homeConnection: Eat together at a table and talk about the day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sit at a table and eat nicely" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A child eating at a table
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Sit and eat, sit and eat, slowly, slowly.

lessons.title: Not wasting food
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will take only what they can eat and say that food is precious.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can care for belongings and use please and thank you.
resources: A plate and a small bowl of toy food
lessons.starter: Show a plate with too much toy food and say "That is too much. We take a little."
teacherActivities: Show how to take a small amount and ask for more.
Show pictures of a farmer growing food and say "Someone worked hard."
Let children serve themselves toy food on a plate.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to take a small amount and ask for more. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Show pictures of a farmer growing food and say "Someone worked hard." Children: Children look and listen.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children serve themselves toy food on a plate. Children: Child takes a little.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We do not waste food." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: A little at a time
practical.safety: Use toy food only for serving practice. Never force a child to finish food and be sensitive to families’ circumstances.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say who grew the food.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.homeConnection: Let your child serve small portions and thank the cook.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "take only what they can eat and say that food is precious" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Snack time practice
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will use all their eating manners at a real or pretend snack time.
successCriteria: Washes hands and sits to eat
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can care for belongings and use please and thank you.
resources: Cups, plates, safe soft snack or toy food
lessons.starter: Say "It is snack time. First wash, then sit, then please and thank you."
teacherActivities: Remind children of the three steps.
Let children wash hands and go to the table.
Serve the snack and say please and thank you.
Clear the plates and say "Well done."
learnerActivities: Children repeat wash, sit and ask.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Remind children of the three steps. Children: Children repeat wash, sit and ask.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children wash hands and go to the table. Children: Children wash and sit.
Step 3. Teacher: Serve the snack and say please and thank you. Children: Child asks and thanks.
Step 4. Teacher: Clear the plates and say "Well done." Children: Child puts a plate away.

practical.title: Snack time
practical.safety: Check every child’s allergies and avoid choking hazards. Keep a second adult nearby and seat children while they eat.

differentiation.support: Sit beside the child and prompt each step.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the snack helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wipe hands and say "Thank you for the food."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep mealtime routines the same at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use all their eating manners at a real or pretend snack time" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 mealtime check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child behaves at mealtimes.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can care for belongings and use please and thank you.
lessons.starter: Sing the snack song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: hand washing, table manners and serving.
At each station watch how the child behaves.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: hand washing, table manners and serving. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child behaves. Children: Child follows with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Mealtime stations
practical.safety: Use toy food only and supervise each station. Keep floors dry and wipe spills.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend table manners.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: washes hands before eating; sits to eat; uses please and thank you; takes a small amount.

questions.question: What do we do before eating?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep good mealtime habits at home.
